objectives: By the end of this course, students will know how to investigate the relationships between school and community contexts and young adolescent learning.

By the end of this course, students will know how to explore opportunities and strategies in order to advocate for young adolescents, middle grades schools/educators, families, communities, and themselves.
Students will understand the unique cognitive, physical, social, emotional, and moral characteristics of young adolescents as individuals and members of groups.
Students will understand how ethnicity, language, religion, socioeconomic status, gender, geographic origin, sexual orientation, and physical and mental exceptionalities may influence student lives.
Students will understand the implications of young adolescent development for successful middle grades programs and schools.
Students will understand how prior learning, differing family background, and diverse cultural backgrounds influence young adolescent learning.
Students will understand the role of interdisciplinary and grade-level team planning in developing curriculum.
Students will use content standards when designing curriculum.
Students will incorporate the ideas, interests, and experiences of young adolescents in curriculum.
topics: Social conditions of children and young adolescents Socio-economic status and the schooling of children and young adoles

objectives: Students will understand the interdisciplinary nature of knowledge and how to make connections among subject areas when planning curriculum.
Students will use content standards when designing curriculum.
Students will teach in ways that develop young adolescents' competence in subject matters and requisite skills.
Students will use effective content-specific teaching strategies.
Students will use a variety of developmentally appropriate teaching/learning strategies and materials and resources that motivate adolescents to learn (e.g., technological resources).
Students will employ effective, developmentally responsive classroom management techniques.
Students will use a variety of formal and informal assessment techniques to assess student learning.
Students will engage in ongoing forms of inquiry about their practice, at the classroom level, the team or grade level, and the school level.
topics: Curriculum Lesson Planning and Unit Planning Teaching Models Middle School Program Characteristics

objectives: Students will explore the various roles of middle grades teachers with emphasis on classroom, team, school, and community issues.
Students will reflect on previous course work.
Students will discuss issues, needs, and concerns related to teaching in the middle grades during induction years.
